original.target_description: Experiment 1 main data: ordinary least squares regression of mean estimated weight for each of 120 female-body photographs on actual stimulus weight, using judgements from 29 women without eating-disorder histories. Positive slope test; contraction-bias slope-versus-one test is separately reported.

n.location: Accepted manuscript pp. 7–9, Stimuli, Procedure and Experiment 1 main data
n.quote: One hundred and twenty digital photographs of female bodies were used as stimuli in this study.
n.sample_role: Stimulus photographs / women depicted, each contributing a mean estimated weight to the OLS regression; 29 female raters are not the regression observation count.
n.exclusions: Potential raters with current or past eating disorders excluded during recruitment. No stimulus exclusions reported; model F(1,118) is consistent with 120 stimulus observations.

es.location: Accepted manuscript p. 10, Experiment 1 main data
es.metric: β1 (unstandardized regression slope, estimated weight on actual weight)

p.location: Accepted manuscript p. 10, Experiment 1 main data

replication.target_description: Healthy controls: regression weight for actual BMI predicting self-estimated BMI, with test of slope less than 1 (contraction bias), in the initial multivariate analysis on published p. 12. This is self-estimation, whereas the original Experiment 1 involved judging other women.

n.sample_role: Healthy-control women in the initial complete-data analysis; excludes the 33 eating-disorder-history participants from this group-specific slope test.
n.exclusions: Participants section states 133 women provided complete datasets on all tasks, comprising 100 controls and 33 women with eating-disorder histories. This is before the later BMI-restricted post-hoc analysis.

es.location: Published p. 12, Multivariate statistics: Controls versus women with an eating disorder history
es.quote: the regression weight for actual BMI was significantly less than 1 for the healthy controls (F1, 97 = 15.24, p < 0.001, β = 0.74, SE = 0.067)
es.metric: β (unstandardized regression weight, self-estimated BMI on actual BMI)

p.location: Published p. 12, healthy-control regression weight compared with 1

reported_success.quote: Consistent with prior research [19–25], healthy controls demonstrated a contraction bias in body size estimation

notes: Both source titles verified: original from Figshare repository full accepted manuscript, replication from publisher full text matching frozen cache. Original locator p.5 is version-dependent: acquired manuscript p.5 discusses the contraction-bias hypothesis, while Experiment 1 main results appear on manuscript pp.9–10. Replication p.12 contains several possible coefficients, and the supplied neutral description does not uniquely identify a predictor/group. Extracted the healthy-control contraction-bias slope as the closest conceptual match to original Experiment 1; target_match remains null on both sides because the sparse locators do not uniquely establish the intended test. Original slope coefficient t test is against zero; the distinct contraction-bias test against one is F(1,118) = 124.18, p < .0001. Replication p belongs to the printed slope-versus-one test for the same 0.74 coefficient, not the overall BMI effect (0.91), BMI-by-group interaction (-0.31), or ED-history slope (0.95). Narrative success is scoped to healthy-control contraction bias, not an unqualified verdict on all eating-disorder findings. No metrics converted.
